issue_context.title: Exceptions silently swallowed in $(fn)
issue_context.body:

Frequently Reported Issues:
  * Selectors with '#' break: See https://github.com/jquery/jquery/issues/2824

### Description

If an exception is thrown in an event handler (such as $.ready), it is silently swalloed.

There are many cases in which exceptions are used to indicate errors for situations that are not code errors, for instance:

``` javascript
var foo = function(arg){
  var result = parseFloat(arg);
  if(isNaN(result)){ 
    throw new Error('not a number');
  }
};
```

Exceptions like that may be cought by the user, such as when the number is user-input. But they may also indicate errors in the usage of the code (such as foo('123') ), in which case catching them is counter productive since they can't be debugged anymore.
### Link to test case

http://jsbin.com/bazaxixihe/edit?html,js,output

review_comments:
We avoid deviating from the standards as well as adding new undocumented parameters to publicly available methods. Also, the current Deferreds API should be enough to achieve the goals of this PR. All we need is to automatically attach a special `.catch` handler to the `readyList.then( fn )` promise in the `core/ready.js` file.
OK, will move to that direction. My concern is though that if we want to provide `$( fn, except )` in API, then public selector call must be modified in `init.js`, as I have done. Should I do it another way?
We definitely don't want to expose new public functionality on Deferred without thinking carefully how it affects things. I think this should be a private API for now. It may be that we need some other implementation. I wonder if we could always use the [no-deferreds](https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/25d8ccd1112d75394b91071ff7eba13283aaf898/src/core/ready-no-deferred.js) implementation, it adds some bulk but that would need to be compared against the size increase here as well.
